chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a Magian who catches fish; is it permissible to eat from it? He said, 'I would not eat it until I look at it.'
Hammad said, meaning until I hear him recite the name (of God).
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What Hammad mentioned in the interpretation of the report is not correct,
because we have previously presented reports indicating that reciting the name (of God) is not required in catching fish.
The meaning of his saying 'until I look at it' is that he looks at the catch to see that it is brought out of the water alive, or is given while it is alive.
Because whenever the Magians or others from the various types of disbelievers give it to you, and it is dead, it is not permissible for him to eat it, nor is their testimony accepted regarding that.
And that which indicates what we said is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish caught by Magians if they did not recite God's name?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the condition 'until I look at it' regarding fish caught by Magians refers to verifying the fish is alive when extracted from water, rather than requiring the recitation of *tasmiyah*. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence as it establishes that the state of the animal (alive vs. dead) at the moment of capture determines permissibility, independent of the catcher's specific ritual invocation. The correction by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan highlights the scholarly method of reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith by prioritizing contextual evidence over literal interpretation of the narrator's understanding.
